Camera-to-IMU rotation (quaternion w, x, y, z)
Focal length along X in pixels for a 640×480 frame. Affects scale and depth.
Focal length along Y in pixels. Usually equal to focal x.
Principal point X. The nominal value is 320; calibration gave 302–310. Try 302 if planes drift sideways.
Principal point Y. The nominal value is 240.
Radial distortion k0. Usually close to zero.
Distortion k1. Usually 0; large values break tracking.
Actual frame readout time from the sensor metadata — 26 763 333 ns (26.76 ms). A wrong value severely breaks depth during motion.
Offset of the camera timestamp relative to the IMU. Negative means the camera is considered “earlier”. Tune using DESYNC logs.
1 — RUNTIME_CHECK_REQUIRED, 2 — TRUSTED_AS_BOOTTIME. Value 2 is usually the right choice.
1 — from the profile, 2 — IMAGE_METADATA. Try 2 if the camera reports readout timestamps.
IMU offset along X in the camera frame. 0 is the safe choice when the real lever arm is unknown.
IMU offset along Z (along the optical axis). Physically no more than ±0.01; larger values are impossible.
W component of the quaternion. ≈ 0.0015 for this mount.
Gyroscope scale along X. ARCore estimates ≈1.03 online.
Gyroscope scale along Y. ARCore estimates ≈1.015.
Gyroscope scale along Z. ARCore estimates ≈1.002.
Accelerometer scale along X. The normal value is ≈ 1.0.
Accelerometer scale along Y. The normal value is ≈ 1.0.
Accelerometer scale along Z. The normal value is ≈ 1.0.
Gyroscope noise. Less means more trust in the IMU, more means more trust in the camera. Generic value 0.0005309.
Initial gyroscope bias along X, rad/s. Measured while stationary.
Initial gyroscope bias along Y, rad/s.
Initial gyroscope bias along Z, rad/s.
Depth API: 1 — disabled, 2 — enabled. Planes use ML depth.

Kalibr calibration
1. The AprilGrid 6×6 is already printed (tagSize ≈ 24.75 mm).
2. Get close: the target should fill MORE THAN HALF of the frame.
3. Start → keep still for the first 5 s.
4. For 60–90 s move smoothly around the target:
 back/forth, left/right, up/down, tilts.
5. Stop.

1. The AprilGrid 6×6 is already printed:
 tagCols=6, tagRows=6, tagSize≈0.02475 m, tagSpacing=0.3.
2. Glue it to a rigid flat backing and put it on a table.
3. Use bright light: the brighter it is, the shorter the exposure and the less motion blur.
4. Get so close that the target fills MORE THAN HALF of the frame
 (about 25–40 cm from the phone). Do not step back!
5. Tap “Start”. Keep the phone still for the first 5 seconds.
6. Then for 60–90 seconds move the phone smoothly around the target:
 back/forth, left/right, up/down, tilts (pitch/yaw/roll).
7. Keep the target in the frame; move slowly, without blur or jerks.
8. Tap “Stop”. The data is saved in the app storage.

Recording is grayscale 1280×960, ~20 frames/s, IMU ~400 Hz.

Export (from a debug build):
adb exec-out run-as io.github.nikonektik.arcoretoolkit tar -c files/calib > calib.tar

Then on your computer: unpack, build a ROS bag and run Kalibr.
